items.question: How must this teaching be guarded in the world of mortals among the lowest of men?
premises: The teaching is to be concealed.
Concealment must be done with effort.
The context is the mortal world among the lowest of men.
items.inference: Therefore this teaching must be carefully kept secret in the mortal world among unworthy people.
items.plain_english: It must be carefully concealed in the mortal world among the lowest of men.

items.question: To whom may this teaching be given after proper testing?
premises: The teaching is to be given.
The recipient should be previously accomplished.
The recipient must be tested for one year.
items.inference: Therefore the teaching may be given only to a previously accomplished person who has been tested for one year.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is already accomplished and has been tested for one year.

items.question: Which chapter concludes in the text that emerged from Candradvīpa?
premises: The text is described as emerged from Candradvīpa.
The section is identified as fifth.
The section is called a chapter.
items.inference: Therefore this marks the fifth chapter in the work emerged from Candradvīpa.
items.plain_english: Thus ends the fifth chapter in the text that emerged from Candradvīpa.

items.question: What understanding has been gained through the grace of the lord of the Kaulas?
premises: The speaker addresses the lord of the Kaulas.
Knowledge has arisen by that lord's grace.
What is known is the determination of the Kaula teaching.
items.inference: Therefore by the lord's grace the speaker has come to know the determination of the Kaula teaching.
items.plain_english: O Lord of the Kaulas, by your grace I have come to know the determination of the Kaula teaching.

items.question: What is the soul that has been declared, and what is its true nature?
premises: The soul has been declared in the teaching.
Its identity is asked about.
Its essential nature is asked about.
items.inference: Therefore the inquiry seeks both the identity and the essential nature of the declared soul.
items.plain_english: Who is that soul that has been declared, and what is the nature of the soul?

items.question: Into what does the soul dissolve, and what complete explanation should be given about this?
premises: The soul's dissolution is in question.
The locus of dissolution is asked about.
A complete explanation is requested.
items.inference: Therefore the teaching must explain fully into what the soul dissolves.
items.plain_english: And into what does it dissolve? Tell me all of that.

items.question: What supreme qualities define the soul in its highest characterization?
premises: The soul is identified as supreme.
The soul is described as partless and eternal.
The soul is described as free from disease and stainless.
items.inference: Therefore the soul is characterized as supreme, partless, eternal, and utterly pure.
items.plain_english: He is supreme, partless, eternal, free from disease, and stainless.

items.question: How is the supreme soul further identified in terms of haṃsa and individual power?
premises: The soul is described as supreme.
That same soul is identified as haṃsa.
That soul is also identified as the individual endowed with power.
items.inference: Therefore the supreme soul is identified as haṃsa, the individual associated with power.
uncertainties: The exact doctrinal sense of śakti+pudgalaḥ is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: That soul is supreme; indeed he is the haṃsa, the individual associated with power.

items.question: Where is the breath-filled vital air said to be situated in living beings?
premises: The subject is the air filled with breath.
This air is described as situated.
Its location is in all beings.
items.inference: Therefore the breath-filled vital air is situated in all living beings.
uncertainties: Agreement of saṃsthitam with vāyuḥ is irregular in form.
items.plain_english: The breath-filled vital air is situated in all living beings.

items.question: What is the soul called immediately upon leaving the body?
premises: The subject is identified as he.
The condition is merely leaving the body.
In that condition he is called supreme Śiva.
items.inference: Therefore upon merely leaving the body, he is declared to be supreme Śiva.
items.plain_english: As soon as he leaves the body, he is called the supreme Śiva.

items.question: How is this teaching said to be received and transmitted according to tradition?
premises: The teaching is heard as abiding in the ear.
It is addressed to the goddess.
It has come down through traditional succession.
items.inference: Therefore the teaching is received aurally and transmitted through an unbroken tradition.
items.plain_english: O Goddess, it is heard in the ear, having come down through the succession of tradition.

items.question: What is the effect of merely hearing this knowledge, as addressed to the fair-faced one?
premises: The knowledge is described as merely heard.
The instrument is this knowledge alone.
The statement is addressed to the fair-faced one.
items.inference: Therefore even mere hearing of this knowledge is presented as efficacious.
uncertainties: The main predicate continues in the next verse.
items.plain_english: O fair-faced one, by this mere knowledge, simply heard...

rows.grounds: object or state associated with renunciation

items.question: What practice over six months leads to a state free from bondage?
premises: A person should practice for six months.
The practice is associated with the ochre state.
The resulting state is free from bondage.
items.inference: Therefore one who practices for six months attains a state free from bondage.
uncertainties: The syntactic role of kāṣāyaṃ is somewhat ambiguous without wider context.
items.plain_english: Whoever practices for six months attains the ochre state, free from bondage.

items.question: What condition and companionship result from the prescribed practice?
premises: The practitioner becomes freed from all diseases.
The practitioner gains association with yogis.
This association is described as union.
items.inference: Therefore the practice results in freedom from all diseases and union with yogis.
items.plain_english: Freed from all diseases, he attains union together with the yogis.

items.question: What teaching has now been communicated to Bhairavī regarding the soul?
premises: The speaker addresses Bhairavī.
Something has been told to her.
What has been told is the practice concerning the soul.
items.inference: Therefore the practice concerning the soul has now been explained to Bhairavī.
items.plain_english: O Bhairavī, this practice concerning the soul has been told to you.

items.question: To what kind of resolved recipient may this teaching be given?
premises: The teaching is to be given.
The recipient is endowed with all states.
The recipient has a resolved mind.
items.inference: Therefore the teaching may be given to one who is fully endowed and firmly resolved.
uncertainties: The case difference between genitive and locative recipients is syntactically unusual.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is endowed with all states and has a firmly resolved mind.

items.question: What Kaula essence must not be given because of its origin among the yoginīs?
premises: There is a Kaula essence.
This essence is connected with the origin of the yoginīs.
It is explicitly not to be given.
items.inference: Therefore the Kaula essence originating from the yoginīs must not be given.
uncertainties: The syntactic relation of sambhavam to sāraṃ is somewhat compressed.
items.plain_english: The Kaula essence, which has its origin in the yoginīs, must not be given.

rows.grounds: subject in accusative-like form in this context

items.question: What transformation of the body is claimed after being struck by the veil of ignorance?
premises: The speaker refers to her own body.
The body was struck by the veil of ignorance.
Now the body is described as pure.
items.inference: Therefore the body, once struck by ignorance, is now declared pure.
uncertainties: The form deham is unexpected for a nominative subject.
items.plain_english: Today my body, once struck by the veil of ignorance, is pure.

items.question: What auspicious method for overcoming time does the speaker now wish to hear?
premises: The speaker now expresses a wish.
The wish is to hear something.
The object is the auspicious deception of time.
items.inference: Therefore the speaker wishes to hear the auspicious means of overcoming time.
items.plain_english: Now I wish to hear the auspicious means of deceiving time.

items.question: What assurance is given about the destruction of death through the teaching to be told?
premises: The speaker declares they will tell.
There is said to be no doubt.
The result described is the destruction of death.
items.inference: Therefore the teaching will explain without doubt how death is destroyed.
items.plain_english: I will tell you; there is no doubt, as to how death is destroyed.

items.question: What condition affects even the wise person at the tip of nectar with its essence?
premises: The location is the tip of nectar.
The essence of juice is involved.
Even a wise person is described as burning.
items.inference: Therefore even the wise may experience a burning condition at the tip of nectar.
uncertainties: The yogic-physiological referent of amṛta+agraṃ is not explicit.
items.plain_english: Even the wise person, at the tip of nectar, is burning with the essence of its juice.

items.question: How should the breath be drawn in at the root of the tongue and palate to counteract time?
premises: The practice is located at the root of the tongue and palate.
The practitioner should take in the air.
The action should be done slowly.
items.inference: Therefore one should slowly draw in the breath at the root of the tongue and palate.
items.plain_english: Placing it at the root of the tongue and palate, one should slowly drink in the breath.

rows.grounds: compound temporal clause with past participle

items.question: What result follows when this practice is performed for one full year?
premises: The practice is performed for one year.
The condition is that it has been practiced.
The stated result is the destruction of old age and death.
items.inference: Therefore practicing for one year destroys old age and death.
items.plain_english: When practiced for one year, old age and death are destroyed.

items.question: What immunity to poison is claimed for the practitioner even when bitten by great serpents?
premises: Poison is the potential threat.
The practitioner may be bitten by great serpents.
Poison does not enter the body.
items.inference: Therefore the practitioner becomes immune to poison even when bitten by great serpents.
items.plain_english: Poison does not enter the body, even if one is bitten by great serpents.
